title: Observability dashboard governance and metric contract playbook
summary: A lightweight governance plan and metric-contract template to reduce dashboard sprawl, clarify ownership, and cap query costs for inference dashboards.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic playbook for governing inference dashboards and metric contracts across Redwood. Goal: reduce duplicate panels, make ownership explicit, define a lightweight metric contract, and add simple trace-sampling guidance to keep investigation signal affordable.

Audience:
- Observability engineers (owners)
- Service/product engineers who create dashboards
- SRE and oncall operators
- Product managers running feature rollouts

Problem statement (why this exists):
- Lots of ad-hoc dashboards created by feature teams; duplication and inconsistent metric names.
- Dashboards are expensive to query (high-cardinality joins, unbounded time ranges).
- Engineers are unsure what to instrument and what counts as a canonical metric.
- Traces are useful but over-collected; retention and sampling costs rising.

Governance at a glance (proposed lightweight model):
1) Ownership: Every dashboard must declare a single owner (person) and an owner team. Owners are responsible for queries, cost, and accuracy.
2) Metric contract: Before new panels are added to a shared dashboard, a one-paragraph metric contract is attached to the dashboard notes (template below).
3) Quarterly audit: Observability guild runs a 15-min audit sprint each quarter to mark stale dashboards and reassign owners.
4) Query cost budget: Dashboards flagged as cross-tenant or long-range must include an estimated query-cost score (Low/Med/High) and an optimization plan if High.
5) Deprecation window: If a dashboard receives no queries for 90 days and owner does not respond to repo/Slack ping, mark as deprecated and schedule removal in 30 days.

Metric contract template (fill these fields, keep it short):
- metric_name: canonical name (snake_case)
- intent: one-sentence purpose (why this metric exists)
- definition: how the metric is computed (source, aggregation window, cardinality knobs)
- primary_sli: yes/no and SLI expression (if applicable)
- owner: person/team
- sampling_and_cardinality_notes: cardinality expectations and recommended tag set (max 3 high-cardinality tags)
- query_cost_estimate: Low | Medium | High (brief rationale)
- acceptance_criteria: list of checks (unit tests, comparison against golden metric)

Example metric contracts (two compact examples):
1) metric_name: inference.request_p95_latency_ms
   intent: Track tail latency for request->final-token across hosted API.
   definition: 95th percentile of request end_time - start_time computed over 5m windows, exclude health-check routes; computed at service level.
   primary_sli: yes; SLI = p95(latency) over 5m rolling
   owner: eng-serving-runtime
   sampling_and_cardinality_notes: limit tag set to [env, model_id]; avoid user_id-level facets. If model_id cardinality > 200, aggregate to model_family.
   query_cost_estimate: Medium (p95 over many shards)
   acceptance_criteria: instrumented in code + dashboard panel has unit tests that assert no drift vs raw histogram.

2) metric_name: kv_cache.hit_rate
   intent: Measure effectiveness of prefix/KV caching for inference workloads.
   definition: hit_rate = hits / (hits + misses) computed per minute, reported per tenant and per region.
   primary_sli: no
   owner: eng-serving-runtime/infra-cache
   sampling_and_cardinality_notes: per-tenant only when tenant traffic > 100 req/min; otherwise report global. Keep tenant tag but limit retention for low-volume tenants.
   query_cost_estimate: Low
   acceptance_criteria: correlates with decreased per-token cost in Optimize reports; automated smoke check in telemetry CI.

Tracing guidance (practical rules for inference traces):
- Span granularity: prefer coarse-grained spans per logical phase (router -> model-infer -> postprocess) and avoid creating per-token spans unless debugging a specific kernel.
- Essential trace tags: request_id, tenant_id (hashed), model_id (family), route, latency_ms, kv_cache_hit (bool), fallback_reason (if any).
- Sensitive data: never include prompt text or full customer identifiers. Hash values if used for linking.
- Sampling policy: default adaptive sampling: 100% sampling for error traces and fallback events; 1–5% baseline sampling for success traces depending on traffic. For heavy tenants we run reservoir sampling per-tenant with a cap of 500 traces/day.
- Retention tiers: keep error/fallback traces 30d, sampled success traces 7d, full debug traces (feature-specific) stored externally on-demand.

Dashboard design rules (notes for authors):
- Single-purpose pages: each dashboard should answer one operational question (e.g., "Model latency by family") not multiple unrelated ones.
- Panel density: aim for 4–8 panels per page; avoid >12.
- Linked drilldowns: include a link to a trace-log or a probe panel for deeper investigation.
- Time-range defaults: 1h for realtime ops; 24h for day-over-day trends. Avoid default 90d unless analytics team explicitly needs it.
- Query knobs: add a panel-level timepicker and a tenant filter with preset buckets (top 10 tenants, aggregated else).

Query cost guardrails (lightweight):
- Prohibit unbounded cardinality in group_by without an archive/aggregation fallback.
- Long-window percentile computations (p99 over 30d) should be pre-aggregated into rollup tables.
- Add a short comment on each expensive panel: why it needs to be expensive and when to run it (ad-hoc vs chart refresh).
- Enforcement: observability CI will run a lint that flags panels with potential O(N^2) joins or large cardinality references.

Oncall and runbook integration:
- Each operational dashboard must include a pinned runbook link and the primary oncall rotation responsible for the first responder.
- Runbook should reference the metric contract and state the immediate triage steps and safe fallbacks (route to lower tier model, degrade features).

Rollout checklist for new dashboards/panels (author follows):
- Draft metric contract in dashboard notes.
- Validate metric against telemetry CI (unit tests or aggregation checks).
- Estimate query_cost and confirm owner.
- Add trace-sampling tag to queries if linking traces is expected.
- Get quick review by observability guild (1–2 people) for cost and cardinality.
- Publish with owner and quarterly audit reminder.

Audit play (observability guild 15-min quarterly):
- Run an automated query for dashboards with zero queries in 90d.
- Ping owners for confirmation; reassign if owner changed teams.
- For High-cost dashboards, request an optimization plan within 30 days.

Open questions and tradeoffs:
- How strict should we be on metric name collisions across teams? (propose a "family" prefix convention but avoid heavy enforcement initially)
- Where to store pre-aggregates for costly percentiles (metrics backend vs specialized OLAP).
- Tiering traces: how to support fast ad-hoc debugging without exploding storage costs?

Next steps (immediate):
- Share this doc with eng-serving-runtime and SRE for comments (1 week).
- Build a metric-contract template PR in the telemetry repo and add to dashboard creation modal (2 sprints).
- Implement a dashboard-linting job in CI to detect obvious high-cardinality panels (3 sprints).

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Add examples for embedding-serving dashboards (embed vector cardinality notes).
- Draft Slack escalation phrasing for pinging dashboard owners.
- Workshop with solutions-engineering to align on customer-facing dashboards.
